mainTopic: Who receives מתנות כהונה (a כֹּהֶנֶת), which animals owe them (כלאים and כוי), and the משנה on exemptions from the gifts
overview: This amud opens with עולא defending his practice of giving מתנות כהונה to a כֹּהֶנֶת. He argues that the מנחה passage had to say 'אהרן ובניו' to limit itself to males. Two ברייתות disagree. דבי רבי ישמעאל leaves out a כֹּהֶנֶת, and דבי רבי אליעזר בן יעקב includes her through מיעוט אחר מיעוט. Several אמוראים ate the gifts through their wives, and מרימר rules that the הלכה follows רב, רב חסדא and עולא, as well as רב אדא בר אהבה about a לויה's son. Next a ברייתא asks whether the gifts apply to a כלאים animal and a כוי. רב הונא בר חייא says the חכמים require only half the gifts because of the doubt about the father. רבי יוחנן says a כוי owes all the gifts, since the word 'אם' includes it directly. Finally a new משנה teaches cases where the gifts are not owed. The first is a בכור mixed in with one hundred animals, and the גמרא begins to challenge that ruling.

steps.title: עולא turns the objection into a proof
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers the challenge from the מנחה of a כהן. That passage says 'אהרן ובניו', so it limits itself to males on purpose. A plain 'כהן' elsewhere therefore includes a כֹּהֶנֶת.
steps.simpleTranslation: From your own objection I bring my proof: 'Aaron and his sons' is written in that passage.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the challenge against his practice of giving gifts to a כֹּהֶנֶת. He says the very source used to attack him actually supports him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the passage about the מנחה, the תורה says 'אהרן ובניו', the sons. This shows the word 'כהן' alone was not enough to leave out daughters. So where the gifts passage just says 'כהן', daughters are included.

keyTerms.meaning: From your burden, meaning from the very point you used to object
The passage or section of the תורה
A female from a כהן family, the daughter of a כהן
A flour offering brought by a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: This is עולא's answer to an objection that came just before this section. It is not a new topic, so read it as the second half of a conversation already going on.

phrases.english: From your burden (your own objection):
phrases.notes: He means: the very point you used to attack me is where my proof comes from.

phrases.english: "Aaron and his sons" are written in the passage.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:7, the passage about the מנחה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection raised against עולא just before this section
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מנחה laws seem to show that 'כהן' means only males, so a כֹּהֶנֶת should not get the gifts.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מנחה passage had to add 'אהרן ובניו' to limit itself to males. So a plain 'כהן' includes a כֹּהֶנֶת.

steps.title: School of רבי ישמעאל: a priest, not a female priest
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל taught that 'כהן' means a male, not a כֹּהֶנֶת. We learn the unclear places from the clear one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'A priest' means a priest and not a female priest. Let the unclear verse be learned from the clear verse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that goes against עולא. It says the gifts are only for male כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Where the תורה says 'אהרן ובניו', it is clear that it means males. רבי ישמעאל's school says that every unclear mention of 'כהן', such as in the gifts, should follow that clear verse. So a כֹּהֶנֶת is left out, which is the opposite of עולא's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of, the students of a particular sage
Unclear, not spelled out
Clear, spelled out explicitly
Let the unclear be learned from the clear

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"A priest" means a priest and not a female priest,
and let the unspecified be learned from the explicit.
phrases.notes: The 'explicit' one is the 'אהרן ובניו' verse from the previous step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a תנאי view that disagrees with עולא's reading
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gifts given to a 'כהן' go only to males. A כֹּהֶנֶת does not receive them.

steps.title: School of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: even a female priest
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי אליעזר בן יעקב taught that the gifts verse includes a כֹּהֶנֶת. It says 'כהן' twice, and two limits in a row make an inclusion.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב taught: 'A priest', and even a female priest. It is a limit after a limit, and a limit after a limit comes only to include.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that supports עולא. It says a כֹּהֶנֶת does receive the gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This school agrees that each 'כהן' by itself would leave out a woman. The gifts verse, however, mentions the כהן twice, so it is two exclusions in a row. By the rule of מיעוט אחר מיעוט, a double exclusion actually includes, so the כֹּהֶנֶת is included.

keyTerms.meaning: A limiting word in a verse that leaves something out
A limiting word after another limiting word
To include, to add more cases

steps.confusionAlert: It sounds backwards, but in this rule two exclusions do not exclude twice as much. Together they include.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא gives a תנאי source for עולא's practice. The next step shows that the אמוראים acted on it.

phrases.aramaic: דְּבֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב תָּנָא:
phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov taught:
"A priest", and even a female priest,
phrases.notes: The verse is דברים 18:3, which mentions the כהנים twice.

phrases.english: it is a limitation after a limitation,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מִיעוּט אַחַר מִיעוּט אֶלָּא לְרַבּוֹת.
phrases.english: and a limitation after a limitation comes only to include.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב תָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite תנאי view, which supports עולא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כֹּהֶנֶת receives the gifts, because the double 'כהן' is a מיעוט אחר מיעוט, which includes.

steps.title: Several אמוראים ate the gifts because of their wives
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא, רב פפא, רב יימר and רב אידי בר אבין all ate מתנות כהונה because their wives were daughters of כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא ate on account of his wife. רב פפא ate on account of his wife. רב יימר ate on account of his wife. רב אידי בר אבין ate on account of his wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports what several אמוראים actually did. They ate the gifts through their wives, who were daughters of כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a כֹּהֶנֶת is entitled to the gifts, her husband may share in them even though he is not a כהן. These stories show that in practice the view including a כֹּהֶנֶת was followed.

keyTerms.meaning: Gifts given to כהנים, here the foreleg, jaw and maw
On account of his wife
The daughter of a כהן

steps.whatToRemember: There are two תנאי views on whether a כֹּהֶנֶת gets the gifts. In practice, the אמוראים followed the inclusive view, as עולא did, and ate the gifts through their wives.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana ate on account of his wife,
Rav Pappa ate on account of his wife,
Rav Yeimar ate on account of his wife,

phrases.aramaic: רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין אָכַל בִּשְׁבִיל אִשְׁתּוֹ.
phrases.english: Rav Idi bar Avin ate on account of his wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the practice that follows the view of דבי רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and עולא
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In practice, a כֹּהֶנֶת receives מתנות כהונה, and her husband may eat them on her account.

steps.title: מרימר's practical rulings on the gifts
steps.stepSummary: רבינא reports that מרימר ruled the הלכה follows רב, רב חסדא and עולא in the earlier discussions about מתנות כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: מרימר told me that the הלכה follows רב, it follows רב חסדא, and it follows עולא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up the earlier discussions by telling us which opinions are the practical הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three separate earlier views are confirmed as the final ruling. The one most connected to what we just learned is עולא: a plain 'כהן' includes a כֹּהֶנֶת, so a כהן's daughter may receive the gifts.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows his opinion
The gifts given to a כהן (here: foreleg, jaw and maw)

steps.whatToRemember: The practical הלכה follows עולא: the daughter of a כהן may receive מתנות כהונה.

phrases.english: Ravina said: Mareimar said to me,
the halakha follows Rav,
and the halakha follows Rav Chisda,
and the halakha follows Ulla.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: אֲמַר לִי מָרִימָר, הִלְכְתָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the earlier discussions and the story of the אמוראים in step 4 into a formal practical ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The practical הלכה follows רב, רב חסדא and עולא in the matters of מתנות כהונה.

steps.title: A Levite woman's firstborn son needs no redemption
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה also follows רב אדא בר אהבה: when a לויה gives birth, her son does not need to be redeemed with five סלעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה follows רב אדא בר אהבה: a Levite woman who gave birth, her son is exempt from the five סלעים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more practical ruling: a firstborn son born to a לויה does not need פדיון הבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the same idea as עולא's ruling: a woman carries the status of her father's family. A לויה counts as a Levite, and a Levite's firstborn is exempt from פדיון הבן.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman from a Levite family (a לוי's daughter)
Redeeming a firstborn son by giving a כהן money
Five silver coins, the amount paid for פדיון הבן

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical ruling people still rely on: a firstborn whose mother is a לויה has no פדיון הבן.

phrases.aramaic: וְהִלְכְתָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: And the halakha follows Rav Adda bar Ahava:
a Levite woman who gave birth –
her son is exempt from the five sela'im.
phrases.notes: The five סלעים are the money for redeeming a firstborn son.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related ruling to the list from step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A firstborn son of a לויה is exempt from פדיון הבן.

steps.title: Do the gifts apply to a mixed-breed animal?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the gifts apply to a כלאים animal and to a כוי. רבי אליעזר says a goat–ewe mix must give the gifts, but a goat–doe mix is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: the foreleg, the jaw and the maw apply to a mixed-breed animal and to a כוי. רבי אליעזר says: a mix that comes from a goat and a ewe must give the gifts; a mix from a male goat and a doe is exempt from the gifts.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. A ברייתא teaches whether the gifts must be given from animals of mixed or unclear species.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says the gifts apply to both a כלאים animal and a כוי, with no split. רבי אליעזר splits it. If both parents are domestic (goat and ewe), the gifts are owed. If one parent is a wild doe, they are not, since the gifts apply only to domestic animals.

keyTerms.meaning: The foreleg, the jaw and the maw: the three parts given to a כהן from a slaughtered animal
Here: an animal born from two different species
An animal whose status is unclear: maybe wild, maybe domestic
A female deer (doe), a wild animal

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: the foreleg, the jaw, and the maw
apply to a mixed-breed animal and to a koy.
phrases.notes: A כוי is an animal we're unsure about, whether it counts as wild or domestic.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: כִּלְאַיִם הַבָּא מִן הָעֵז וּמִן הָרָחֵל –
phrases.english: a mixed breed that comes from a goat and a ewe –
is obligated in the gifts,
one from a male goat and a doe –
is exempt from the gifts.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַזְּרוֹעַ וְהַלְּחָיַיִם וְהַקֵּבָה נוֹהֲגִים בְּכִלְאַיִם וּבְכוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the rulings in steps 5–6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא says the gifts apply to כלאים and כוי. רבי אליעזר says a goat–ewe mix owes the gifts, but a male goat–doe mix is exempt.

steps.title: Setting up a difficulty: the only real case of their argument
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls that the only case where רבי אליעזר and the Rabbis argue about covering blood and the gifts is a deer that mated with a female goat. In that case, both sides are unsure whether the father's species counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, we have established that for covering the blood and for the gifts, you only find their argument in a deer that mated with a female goat. And both רבי אליעזר and the Rabbis are unsure whether we take the father's seed into account or not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a question on the ברייתא. It reminds us of an earlier rule, and the actual difficulty comes in step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא showed that their argument only matters when the mother is a domestic goat and the father is a wild deer. Even then, neither side is sure whether the father's wild species counts. This background will make the ברייתא's wording hard to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Now, after all...': opens a point we already know, to build a challenge
The מצוה to cover the blood of a slaughtered wild animal or bird
Do we take the father's species into account?
They are unsure about it

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא has finished its question here. 'מכדי' only lays out the background; the punchline comes next.

phrases.english: Now, we have established
that regarding covering the blood and the gifts
you do not find it
phrases.notes: 'It' means the argument between רבי אליעזר and the Rabbis.

phrases.english: except with a deer that mated with a female goat,
and both for Rabbi Eliezer and for the Rabbis
it is uncertain to them
whether we take the father's seed into account,
or whether we do not take it into account.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings in an earlier rule to set up a challenge to the ברייתא of step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים' ruling in the ברייתא of step 7 that a mixed animal is fully obligated in the gifts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The only real case of the argument is a deer father with a goat mother, and both sides are unsure whether the father's species counts. So the father's half stays a doubt even for the חכמים, and it is hard to see how they can obligate all the gifts. Steps 9–10 complete the question.

steps.title: What the dispute is really about: is a partial sheep still a 'sheep'?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים hold that 'שה' includes even an animal that is only partly a sheep. רבי אליעזר holds it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue about whether 'sheep' includes even a partial sheep. One side says yes, even a partial sheep counts. The other side says we do not include a partial sheep.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 8 showed that both sides are unsure about the father's species, so that cannot be their argument. Here the גמרא names the real argument, and this sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mixed animal is at least partly a sheep, because of its mother. The question is whether the word 'שה' in the פסוק of the gifts covers an animal that is only part sheep. The חכמים say yes and רבי אליעזר says no.

keyTerms.meaning: A sheep or goat. This is the word the תורה uses when it commands the gifts.
Part of a sheep: an animal that is only partly a sheep or goat.
They argue about it.

phrases.english: And they argue about whether 'sheep' includes even a partial sheep:
phrases.notes: The word 'sheep' comes from the פסוק about the gifts (דברים 18:3).

phrases.english: One Sage holds: 'sheep' means even a partial sheep,
phrases.notes: This first view is the חכמים.

phrases.english: and one Sage holds:
we do not say that 'sheep' includes even a partial sheep.
phrases.notes: This second view is רבי אליעזר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the real point of dispute, after step 8 showed that both sides share the doubt about the father.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים: 'שה' includes a partial sheep. רבי אליעזר: it does not.

steps.title: Then the כהן should only get half the gifts
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר's exemption makes sense. But for the חכמים, the father's part is still uncertain, so the owner should be able to keep half the gifts until the כהן brings proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that רבי אליעזר exempts, since he holds a partial sheep does not count. But for the חכמים, even if a partial sheep counts, the כהן should take only half. For the other half, the owner can say: 'Prove that we do not worry about the father's species, and then take it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the חכמים, who said a mixed animal is fully 'obligated'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother's half is clearly sheep, so it surely owes gifts. The father's half is in doubt. When something is in doubt, the owner can refuse to pay until the כהן proves his claim. So the חכמים should require only half the gifts, not all of them.

keyTerms.meaning: It is understandable for... The גמרא uses it to set up a contrast with a view that is harder to explain.
Even granting that...
Half.
The father's seed: the father's species.
Bring proof.

phrases.english: Granted, Rabbi Eliezer, who exempts,
holds 'sheep' but not a partial sheep.
But according to the Rabbis,
even granting that they hold
that 'sheep' includes even a partial sheep,
let him take half,
phrases.notes: 'Him' means the כהן receiving the gifts.

phrases.english: and for the other half, let the owner say to him:
Bring proof
that we are not concerned about the father's species, and then take it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the dispute named in step 9 to attack the חכמים' word 'obligated'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים' ruling in the ברייתא (step 7) that a mixed animal is obligated in the gifts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The father's half is a doubt. In a doubt the owner can demand proof, so only half the gifts should be owed.

steps.title: Yes, the חכמים meant half the gifts
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חייא explains that 'obligated' in the ברייתא means obligated in half the gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חייא said: what does 'obligated' mean when they said it? Obligated in half the gifts.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בר חייא answers the question by agreeing with it. The חכמים never meant all the gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed 'obligated' meant full gifts. רב הונא בר חייא reads the word more narrowly: the owner owes only the certain half. That fits the reasoning from the question perfectly.

keyTerms.meaning: Obligated.
Half of the gifts given to the כהן.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב הונא בר חייא, the חכמים require a mixed animal to give only half the gifts, because the father's part is in doubt.

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Chiya said:
What does 'obligated' mean when they said it?
Obligated in half of the gifts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא: מַאי חַיָּיב נָמֵי דְּקָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10.

steps.title: רבי זירא brings the ברייתא about the כוי
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא opens his challenge with a ברייתא: a כוי is like a בהמה in some ways, like a חיה in others, and like both in others.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא objects from a ברייתא: a כוי has some ways in which it is like a domesticated animal, some ways in which it is like a wild animal, and some ways in which it is like both.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא begins to challenge רב הונא בר חייא's answer. He starts by quoting the opening of a ברייתא, so this is the setup for his point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כוי is an animal whose status is uncertain: we do not know if it is a בהמה or a חיה. Like the mixed animal, it involves a doubt. So how the ברייתא treats its gifts will test רב הונא בר חייא's 'half the gifts' answer.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal whose status as בהמה or חיה is uncertain.
A domesticated animal.
A wild animal.
Ways in which it is the same as...

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira raises an objection:

phrases.aramaic: כּוֹי – יֵשׁ בּוֹ דְּרָכִים שָׁוִין לַבְּהֵמָה,
phrases.english: A כוי has ways in which it is like a domesticated animal,
and ways in which it is like a wild animal,

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ דְּרָכִים שָׁוִין לַחַיָּה וְלַבְּהֵמָה.
phrases.english: and ways in which it is like both a wild animal and a domesticated animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge to the answer of step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא בר חייא's claim that 'obligated' means half the gifts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא about the כוי, another doubtful animal, will be used to test whether 'obligated' can mean only half.

steps.title: The ברייתא's details: the כוי owes the gifts
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists the rules. Its fat is forbidden like a בהמה's. Its blood must be covered like a חיה's. Its blood and גיד הנשה are forbidden like both. It is obligated in the foreleg, jaw and maw. רבי אליעזר exempts.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? Its fat is forbidden like a domesticated animal's fat. Its blood must be covered like a wild animal's blood. In the ways it is like both, its blood and its sciatic nerve are forbidden, just as for both kinds of animal. It is obligated in the foreleg, the jaw and the maw. רבי אליעזר exempts it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא spells out the rules of the כוי, ending with the gifts. רבי זירא is setting up his point: the חכמים here say the כוי is 'obligated' in the gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the כוי is a doubt, it gets the strict side of both categories: its fat is forbidden and its blood must be covered. On the gifts, the ברייתא uses the same word, 'obligated', with רבי אליעזר again exempting. רבי זירא will use this wording against the 'half the gifts' answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden fat. It is forbidden in a בהמה but not in a חיה.
Covering the blood after slaughter. It is required for a חיה but not for a בהמה.
The sciatic nerve, which is forbidden to eat.
The foreleg, the jaw and the maw: the three gifts given to the כהן.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up חֵלֶב (forbidden fat) with חָלָב (milk). Here it means the forbidden fat.

phrases.english: How so?
Its fat is forbidden like the fat of a domesticated animal,
and one must cover its blood, like the blood of a wild animal.
The ways in which it is like both a domesticated and a wild animal:
its blood and its sciatic nerve are forbidden, like those of a domesticated or wild animal,
and it is obligated in the foreleg, the jaw and the maw,
and Rabbi Eliezer exempts it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא that רבי זירא began quoting in step 12. He makes his actual point in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כוי gets the strict rules of both בהמה and חיה, and is 'obligated' in the gifts. רבי אליעזר exempts it.

steps.title: Why didn't the ברייתא say 'half the gifts'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא completes his challenge: if the חכמים only obligate half the gifts, the ברייתא should have said so.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is true that the meaning is half, the ברייתא should have said 'obligated in half the gifts'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא finishes the challenge he began with the ברייתא about the כוי. He argues that the ברייתא's wording does not fit רב הונא בר חייא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא בר חייא said that 'obligated' means obligated in only half the gifts. But the ברייתא just says 'obligated', with no mention of half. A ברייתא that meant half should have said half.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is so (if your explanation is correct)
Half of the gifts given to the כהן
It should have said

phrases.english: And if it is so,
phrases.notes: Meaning: if רב הונא בר חייא is right that the ברייתא means only half the gifts.

phrases.english: it should have said: obligated in half the gifts!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אִיתָא, חַיָּיב בַּחֲצִי מַתָּנוֹת מִבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא quoted in steps 12–13 to attack רב הונא בר חייא's answer in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא בר חייא's reading that 'obligated' means half the gifts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's plain wording says 'obligated' without limiting it, so it should have said 'half' if half was meant.

steps.title: The ברייתא avoided 'half' because of fat and blood
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא could not say 'half' about the fat and blood, so it did not say 'half' about the gifts either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the ברייתא taught about its fat and blood, where it could not say 'half', it did not say 'half' for the gifts either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא בר חייא. It explains why the ברייתא left out the word 'half'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All its forbidden fat is prohibited because of the doubt, and all its blood needs covering. Neither rule can be split into halves here. The ברייתא kept one style through its list, so it did not write half for the gifts, although this answer still means half.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it already taught (one thing, it kept the same style for the next)
Its fat and its blood
Because of that

phrases.english: Since it taught 'its fat and its blood',
where it cannot teach 'half' and 'half',
for that reason it does not teach 'half' (about the gifts).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's challenge in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic explanation of the ברייתא's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Leaving out 'half' proves the ברייתא meant all the gifts.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא kept one uniform wording because 'half' could not apply to fat and blood. 'Obligated' can still mean half the gifts.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב הונא בר חייא, the חכמים obligate a כוי in only half the gifts. The ברייתא left out 'half' only to keep its style the same.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a כוי owes all the gifts
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports that רבי יוחנן says that according to the חכמים, a כוי is obligated in all of the gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said that רבי יוחנן said: according to the חכמים, a כוי is obligated in all the gifts.
steps.whatsHappening: A new opinion arrives from ארץ ישראל through רבין. It disagrees with the 'half' approach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא בר חייא said the חכמים require only half the gifts. רבי יוחנן says they require the full set. His proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: In all of the gifts

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: When רבין came, he said that רבי יוחנן said:
A כוי, according to the Rabbis, is obligated in all the gifts,

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the question of step 10. It says the full gifts are owed, not half.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, the owner of a כוי must give all the gifts.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two opinions. רב הונא בר חייא says the חכמים require half the gifts. רבי יוחנן says they require all of them.

steps.title: The extra word 'אם' includes the כוי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the extra word 'אם' in the פסוק that a hybrid and a כוי are both included in the gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: the פסוק could have said just 'ox'. Why does it say 'whether an ox'? To include a hybrid. It could have said just 'sheep'. Why does it say 'or a sheep'? To include a כוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רבי יוחנן's ruling. A ברייתא learns from an extra word in the פסוק that the כוי is included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אם' is not needed to say 'ox' or 'sheep', so it comes to add something. The extra word puts the כוי directly into the obligation. That means the doubt is gone, so all the gifts are owed and not just half.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the פסוק need to say this?
To include
A hybrid, the offspring of two different species

phrases.english: As it is taught: 'ox' (would have been enough),
why does the verse say 'whether an ox'?
To include the hybrid.
'Sheep' (would have been enough); why does the verse say 'or a sheep'?
To include the כוי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי יוחנן's statement in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that the חכמים obligate a כוי in all the gifts.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading the extra word 'אם' in 'אם שור אם שה' (דברים 18:3).
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the כוי owes all the gifts. Its obligation comes from a direct inclusion in the פסוק, not from a doubt.

steps.title: What does רבי אליעזר learn from 'אם'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר exempts the כוי, so what does he do with the word 'אם'?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר, why does he need this word 'אם'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the other side. רבי אליעזר does not include the כוי, so what does he learn from the extra word?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every extra word in the תורה must teach something. If רבי אליעזר does not use 'אם' to include the כוי, he must use it for something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it?

phrases.english: And רבי אליעזר, why do I need this 'whether'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how רבי אליעזר reads the word explained in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי אליעזר learns from the word 'אם'.

steps.title: 'אם' teaches that the ox and the sheep are separate
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר uses 'אם' to teach that an ox alone or a sheep alone is enough to obligate the gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it to separate them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אליעזר uses 'אם' to split ox and sheep into separate cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this word, someone might think the gifts are owed only after slaughtering both an ox and a sheep. 'אם' shows that each animal obligates the gifts on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: To separate (each item counts on its own)

phrases.english: He needs it to separate (ox from sheep).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אליעזר uses 'אם' to teach that ox and sheep each obligate the gifts on their own.

steps.title: Where do the חכמים learn to separate?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים use 'אם' for the כוי, so where do they learn that each animal counts separately?
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים, where do they learn to separate?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the same question back to the חכמים. They already used 'אם' for the כוי, so they need another source for separating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that one animal alone obligates the gifts. Since the חכמים use 'אם' for including, they need a different word to teach this.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do they know it?

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, from where do they learn to separate?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 18 for the other side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The חכמים' source for separating ox from sheep.

steps.title: The חכמים learn it from 'מאת זובחי הזבח'
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים learn from 'מאת זובחי הזבח' that even one animal obligates the gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: They learn it from 'from those who slaughter a slaughtering'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the חכמים a different source in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'זבח' is singular, one slaughtered animal. So any single slaughter obligates the gifts, and 'אם' is free to include the כוי.

keyTerms.meaning: They derive it
From those who slaughter a slaughtering (דברים 18:3)

phrases.english: They derive it from 'from those who slaughter a slaughtering'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים learn that each animal counts separately from 'מאת זובחי הזבח'.

steps.title: What does רבי אליעזר learn from 'מאת זובחי הזבח'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי אליעזר uses the phrase the חכמים used.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר, what does he do with 'from those who slaughter a slaughtering'?
steps.whatsHappening: Now רבי אליעזר has a phrase left over. The גמרא asks what he learns from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר learned separating from 'אם'. So the phrase 'מאת זובחי הזבח' must teach him something else.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? (what does he learn from it)

phrases.english: And רבי אליעזר, this 'from those who slaughter a slaughtering',
what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, הַאי ״מֵאֵת זוֹבְחֵי הַזֶּבַח״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 21 and asks the parallel question about רבי אליעזר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי אליעזר learns from 'מאת זובחי הזבח'.

steps.title: The claim is made against the butcher
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר uses the phrase for רבא's rule: the כהן claims the gifts from the butcher.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for רבא's teaching, as רבא said: the claim is made against the butcher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אליעזר learns רבא's rule from this phrase, and this closes the back-and-forth about the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'those who slaughter', so the one who does the slaughtering is the person responsible. The כהן brings his claim for the gifts against the butcher, even if the animal belongs to someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: For the teaching of רבא
The legal claim is against the butcher

steps.whatToRemember: Each side uses both phrases of the פסוק. The חכמים: 'אם' includes the כוי, and 'מאת זובחי הזבח' separates. רבי אליעזר: 'אם' separates, and 'מאת זובחי הזבח' teaches that the claim is against the butcher.

phrases.english: He needs it for that of רבא,
as רבא said: the claim is against the butcher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אליעזר learns רבא's rule from the phrase: the כהן claims the gifts from the butcher.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבא's rule has a practical result: the כהן collects the gifts from the one who slaughters.

steps.title: A firstborn animal mixed in with one hundred others
steps.stepSummary: A בכור mixed in with one hundred animals: if one hundred people slaughter them, all are exempt from the gifts. If one person slaughters them all, only one animal is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: A בכור got mixed in with one hundred regular animals. If one hundred different people each slaughter one, every animal is exempt from the gifts. If one person slaughters them all, he is exempt for one animal only.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches what happens to the gifts when a בכור, which does not owe the gifts, gets lost among regular animals that do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When each animal belongs to a different person, each owner can say, 'Maybe mine is the בכור,' so no one has to give. When one person owns them all, he surely has only one בכור among them, so only one animal is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn animal; it is exempt from the gifts
Got mixed in
We exempt
The gifts given to the כהן: foreleg, jaw and maw

phrases.english: MISHNA: A firstborn animal that got mixed in with one hundred others,
when one hundred people slaughter all of them,
we exempt all of them.
If one person slaughters all of them,
we exempt one animal for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins after the earlier discussion of רבי אליעזר and the חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A doubtful בכור exempts every animal when each has a different owner, but only one animal when there is a single owner.

steps.title: Slaughtering for a כהן or a גוי, and partnerships
steps.stepSummary: An animal slaughtered for a כהן or a גוי is exempt from the gifts. A partner of theirs must mark the animal. If a כהן sold an animal 'except for the gifts,' the buyer is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone slaughters an animal for a כהן or a גוי, it is exempt from the gifts. A Jew who shares ownership with them must mark the animal. If the seller said 'except for the gifts,' the buyer does not have to give them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with more cases where the gifts are not given, because of who owns the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gifts are owed only by a regular Jewish owner. A כהן or a גוי does not owe them. A partner must mark the animal so that people seeing it will not think a Jew is skipping the gifts. When the gifts were never sold to the buyer, they are not his to give.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jew
Becomes a partner
That he should mark it
Except for the gifts

phrases.english: One who slaughters for a כהן or for a gentile
is exempt from the gifts.
And one who is a partner with them
must mark it.
And if he said: 'except for the gifts,'
he is exempt from the gifts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more exemptions to the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animals owned by a כהן or a גוי are exempt from the gifts. A partner must mark the animal. A sale 'except for the gifts' leaves the buyer exempt.

steps.title: Buying a cow's innards that contain the gifts
steps.stepSummary: If someone buys a cow's innards and the gifts are among them, he gives the gifts to the כהן. If he bought for one price, he does not reduce what he pays. If he bought by weight, he does reduce it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says, 'Sell me the innards of a cow,' and the gifts are in them, he gives the gifts to the כהן and does not lower the price. If he bought them by weight, he gives them to the כהן and subtracts their value from the price.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a money question: who loses the value of the gifts, the buyer or the seller?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Either way, the gifts go to the כהן. The only difference is the money. With one price for the whole set of innards, the buyer takes the loss. When he pays by weight, he paid for the gifts' weight too, so he takes that amount off the bill.

keyTerms.meaning: Its innards
Deducts
The price, the money
By weight

steps.whatToRemember: In every case of this משנה, the question is whether there is really an owner who owes the gifts, and who carries their cost.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: ״מְכוֹר לִי בְּנֵי מֵעֶיהָ שֶׁל פָּרָה״,
phrases.english: If he said: 'Sell me the innards of a cow,'
and the gifts were among them,
he gives them to the כהן
and does not deduct their value from the price.
If he bought them from him by weight,
he gives them to the כהן
and deducts their value from the price.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְכוֹר לִי בְּנֵי מֵעֶיהָ שֶׁל פָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final case of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The gifts always go to the כהן. A buyer who paid by weight deducts their value, and a buyer who paid one price does not.

steps.title: Why can't the כהן say 'either way, it's mine'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the first case: the כהן should be able to say, 'If it is a בכור, it is all mine; if not, give me my gifts.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Why are they exempt? The כהן can come at him from both sides: 'If this is a בכור, the whole animal is mine. If it is not, give me my gifts.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and challenges the משנה's first case, where all one hundred owners were exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה exempted each owner because maybe his animal is the בכור. But a בכור belongs to the כהן, so the doubt should not help the owner at all. Either way the כהן is owed something, so why should he get nothing?

keyTerms.meaning: But why?
From two sides, an 'either way' claim
My gifts

steps.confusionAlert: The כהן is not claiming the animal is a בכור. He is saying that whichever way the doubt turns out, he is owed something.

phrases.english: GEMARA: But why are they exempt?
Let the כהן come at him from two sides,
and say to him:
If it is a firstborn,
all of it is mine;
and if it is not a firstborn,
give me my gifts.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? יָבֹא עָלָיו כֹּהֵן מִשְּׁנֵי צְדָדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה's first case and attacks its ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that all one hundred owners are exempt from the gifts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The doubt should not help the owner, because the כהן wins both ways: the whole animal if it is a בכור, or the gifts if it is not.
